newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes fall on Feb contract rollovers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes fall on Feb contract rollovers.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes fell late Tuesday as traders rolled over February positions into March on the day the NYMEX prompt month contract expired.
February WTI/Cushing closed the month at $24.75-85 a barrel, down 30 cents from late Monday's cash market.
The spread between February and March WTI stood around 60 cents, although the roll seemed to be narrowing in late-day talk to around 30-40 cents a barrel.
Grade business picked up from this morning's sluggishness. Light Louisiana Sweet was holding at five to 10 cents premium a barrel to WTI/Cushing.
WTI/Midland weakened further, trading at a 40 cents a barrel discount to WTI/Cushing, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was subdued with WTI/Cushing minus 65 cents last heard offered.
West Texas Sour/Midland was rumored to have changed hands at a discount of $1.79 a barrel, although the deal could not be confirmed.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus traded as low as $2.10 a barrel before bouncing back to $2.20-30 a barrel.

Separately, the American Petroleum Institute (API) will issue its weekly inventory report one day late on Wednesday, January 22, after 1630 EST (2130 GMT), as a result of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday on Monday.
The government's Energy Information Administration has also postponed its weekly report by one day to Thursday, January 23, at 0900 EST (1400 GMT).
